title: Canonical complexes, components, shifted iteration and augmentation for character lifts
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring and $G$ a profinite group with the coefficient sizes of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $D$ be a resolution of [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution]. Let $P$ be the underlying nonnegative chain complex, extended along $n\mapsto-n$ to a cochain complex. Identify $P^{-n}$ with $D_n$ by the extension isomorphism. For a map $F:P\to P[q]$ its transported component is $D_{n+q}\to D_n$. For a condensed additive character of [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class], IsLift means equivariance of these components and the formula $[g_0,\dots,g_{n+1}]\mapsto a(g_0^{-1}g_1)[g_1,\dots,g_{n+1}]$ on every profinite parameter. Let $H$ be internal functions and $B$ an inhomogeneous bar diagram of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Define the augmented component by composition with the shifted augmentation and the degree-q inhomogeneous component by the single-object and bar-term isomorphisms. Given a family $L_a:P\to P[1]$, construct $F_{[]}$ as the zero-shift identity and $F_{a++[b]}=F_a;L_b[|a|]$ followed by the shift-addition identification $P[1][|a|]\cong P[|a|+1]$. Construct $e:P\to A[0]$ by extending the given chain augmentation and the canonical extended-single isomorphism. Then its transported zero component is the given augmentation, any degree-one map has zero component at degree zero, and $e[q]F$ has zero components away from degree $-q$. These are actual constructions, with no choice of data from an existence theorem.

proof.text: Use ChainComplex.of for the given boundary maps; extend along embeddingDownNat and use extendXIso to define the term and component identifications.
Define orderedIterate by List.reverseRec with the zero-shift identity and the displayed shifted composition. List.reverseRec_nil and List.reverseRec_concat prove its two recursion equations.

Use ChainComplex.toSingle₀Equiv with boundary_augmentation to construct the chain augmentation. Extend it and apply extendSingleIso. The two component formulas and inverse-hom cancellation give its normalization.

The extension is zero in all positive degrees. Hence a degree-one map has zero target in degree zero. A shifted single complex has zero target outside its single degree, proving the sole-component assertion.
